en: The *Buddha-spoken Maṇidhāri-devī Bodhisattva Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
He was accompanied by one thousand two hundred and fifty great arhats,
as well as an immeasurable multitude of great bodhisattvas,
including Maitreya Bodhisattva.
With the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī and the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara as their leaders.
Accompanied by Mārīcī and other devas,
and surrounded before and behind by the eight classes of beings including the nāgas,
Śāriputra then rose from his seat.
Baring his right shoulder and placing his right knee on the ground,
he joined his palms toward the Buddha and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Bhagavān, in future ages,
what dharma should sentient beings of the final period practice to be liberated from all hardships?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively!
I shall now explain this matter for you.
At that time, the assembly rejoiced and leaped for joy.
He again exhorted the Buddha.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"Previously, there was a deva."
She is named Mārīcī;
she possesses the dharma of great supernatural powers and mastery,
and constantly travels before the sun.
The sun does not see it;
it is that which can see the sun.
No person is able to see it.
No one can know it;
no one can grasp it;
no one can harm it.
No one can deceive them;
no one can bind them;
and no one can claim their wealth and property as a debt.
"No one can punish him;
no enemy can find an opportunity against him.
Thus the Buddha told the bhikṣus.
If there is anyone who knows the name of that goddess Mārīcī,
that person cannot be seen, nor can they be known;
they cannot be seized, nor can they be harmed.
Furthermore, one will not be deceived by others, nor bound by others;
one's wealth and property will not be seized by others,
nor will one be subject to punishment by others.
Furthermore, enemies will not be able to find an opportunity against them.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
"If a son of good family or a daughter of good family knows the name of that goddess Mārīcī..."
One should speak thus: "I,
the disciple so-and-so, because I know the name of that goddess Mārīcī,
no one will be able to see me."
No one can know me;
no one can seize me;
no one can harm me.
No one can deceive me;
no one can bind me;
no one can claim my wealth as a debt.
No one can punish me,
nor can any enemy find an opportunity against me;
this mantra possesses great supernatural power.
It accomplishes all undertakings and destroys all evils.
If it is used for boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*), no evil whatsoever within a hundred *yojanas* will dare to enter.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this incantation:

Namo buddhāya (1) Namo dharmāya (2) Namo saṃghāya (3) Tadyathā (4) Aragamasī (5) Maragamasī (6) Sutumasī (7) Cipramasī (8) Mahācipramasī (9) Mārīcīyamasi (10) Ātatanayamasi (11) Namo citte (12) Svāhā (13) May I be protected amidst royal perils.
Protect me amidst the perils of bandits;
protect me on the road;
protect me in the wilderness when I have lost my way.
Protect me by day;
protect me by night;
protect me amidst the perils of water.
Protect me amidst the danger of fire;
protect me amidst the danger of rākṣasas;
protect me amidst the danger of ḍākinī spirits.
May the poison not strike me;
may the Buddha protect me by his word of truth.
May the Dharma protect me by its word of truth.
May the Sangha protect me through truthful speech.
May the devas protect me through truthful speech.
May the ṛṣis protect me through truthful speech.

Tadyathā: (1) Ara-kule, (2) Ara-kule, (3) Kṛti, (4) Sarvakārhe, (5) Sabodhutejhe, (6) Sarva-idupadāravhe, (7) Rakṣa rakṣa [inserting one’s own name here], (8) Svāhā. This is the incantation for inviting the goddess Mārīcī.
The first is called the Body-Mantra of Mārīcī.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namo ratnatrayāya. Mārīci-ṛddhaye. Māpadeśamayi. Tadyathā. Varale. Vadhale. Varāhamukhi. Sarvatucchati. Vandha vandha. Svāhā.* The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
If there are those who recognize that Bodhisattva Mārīcī,
all obstacles and difficulties— such as the perils of kings, the perils of bandits,
and the perils of fierce beasts and venomous insects— will be eliminated.
Regarding the perils of water, fire,
and so forth: for anyone who wishes to practice this dharma,
among all dharmas, this dharma is the most supreme.
For one who maintains this mantra, even within a hundred yojanas,
no ghosts, spirits, or evil persons shall be able to find an opportunity against them.
This applies even when traveling through difficult terrain.
Rising at dawn, recite the mantra for the previous body.
With this mantra, consecrate a handful of water and sprinkle it in the four directions as well as upon yourself.
Whether on the lapel of the robe, the sleeve, or a corner of the *kāṣāya*,
perform one binding for each incantation, making a total of three knots.
Then proceed into the difficult terrain, reciting the two preceding great mantras continuously as you go.
All those who were commanders of the army guarding against all manner of calamities were completely deluded and intoxicated;
none of them possessed any awareness or knowledge.
After the Buddha had spoken this sutra, [he sat in silence].
I address all the bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs,
the upāsakas and upāsikās,
as well as kings, ministers, and the common people.
If one hears this *Mārīcī-devī-dhāraṇī* spoken by the Buddha and receives and upholds it with single-minded devotion,
that person shall not be harmed by any evil whatsoever.
"O bhikṣus, if there is anyone who can write it down, read it, recite it, or uphold it,
or even place it within their topknot,"
If it is worn within one's clothing and follows the body wherever one goes,
all evils will completely retreat and disperse, with none daring to confront them.
These fourfold assemblies, along with the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings, prostrated before the Buddha and withdrew.
Rejoicing, they practiced accordingly.
This concludes the *Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Mārīcī* as spoken by the Buddha.
